name: Jira
description: Wakes an agent when a Jira Cloud issue changes status, and lets it read what happened, comment, rewrite the description and move the ticket on. A Team Admin binds their team's Jira site and API token and configures which projects to watch and which status transitions matter (e.g. "In Progress → Ready for Dev"); the broker sidecar holds that credential and polls Jira server-side, so the token never reaches your browser or an agent container. On a matching transition the broker wakes the granted agents and queues the event; the agent drains the queue with the `aee-jira inbox` command-line tool and acts with `aee-jira comment` / `update` / `transition`. This replaces the reverted built-in Jira integration (PR #1539) with an installable, uninstallable plugin — removing it leaves the platform byte-identical. Jira Server / Data Center is not supported; there is no two-way sync.

credentials.description: Jira Cloud site — a bare subdomain ("acme") or a full origin ("https://acme.atlassian.net")
Atlassian account e-mail — the Basic-Auth username for the API token
Jira API token — held only by the broker sidecar, never returned after it is set

events.name: status_changed
events.description: A watched issue moved to another status

payload.description: the status the issue moved into

promptLine: When a watched Jira issue changes status you are woken; then work it with `aee-jira`: `aee-jira inbox` (the queued status changes — `--consume` drains them, use it once per wake), `aee-jira list --project KAN [--status "Ready for Dev"]`, `aee-jira show KAN-6`, `aee-jira comment KAN-6 --body "…"`, `aee-jira transition KAN-6 --to "In Progress"`, `aee-jira update KAN-6 --description "…"` (replaces the whole description — keep what the human wrote and add your section; the previous text stays in Jira's history). A transition you make is itself a status change and wakes whichever teammate's trigger names that target status. All Jira access is server-side in the broker; you never see the Jira token.
